title: O ônibus errado
text:
Hoje foi o primeiro dia de Mariana no emprego novo, uma loja de roupas no centro de São Paulo. Ela acordou às seis horas, tomou banho e colocou uma blusa nova. Depois, tomou um café rápido e saiu de casa muito animada.

No ponto, um ônibus chegou logo. Mariana entrou, sentou perto da janela e ficou olhando a cidade. Mas, depois de quarenta minutos, ela não reconheceu nenhuma rua. Então, perguntou ao motorista: “Este ônibus vai para o centro?” Ele respondeu: “Não, moça. Vai para o aeroporto!” Mariana ficou nervosa. Ela desceu no ponto seguinte e ligou para a chefe, dona Sílvia. Pediu desculpas e explicou o problema.

Dona Sílvia riu e disse: “Calma! No meu primeiro dia, eu também peguei o ônibus errado.” Mariana chegou à loja uma hora atrasada, mas o dia foi ótimo, e os colegas foram muito simpáticos. Amanhã, ela vai sair de casa mais cedo e vai ler o número do ônibus duas vezes.
translation:
Today was Mariana's first day at her new job, a clothes shop in downtown São Paulo. She woke up at six o'clock, took a shower and put on a new blouse. Then she had a quick coffee and left home very excited.

At the stop, a bus came right away. Mariana got on, sat by the window and watched the city. But after forty minutes, she didn't recognize a single street. So she asked the driver: “Does this bus go downtown?” He answered: “No, miss. It goes to the airport!” Mariana got nervous. She got off at the next stop and called her boss, Dona Sílvia. She apologized and explained the problem.

Dona Sílvia laughed and said: “Relax! On my first day, I took the wrong bus too.” Mariana arrived at the shop an hour late, but the day was great, and her coworkers were very friendly. Tomorrow, she is going to leave home earlier and read the bus number twice.

questions.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: A bus driver who gets lost in São Paulo
Mariana's first day at a new job
How Mariana found a job at a big bank
Dona Sílvia's first day at a clothes shop
questions.explain: The story begins 'Hoje foi o primeiro dia de Mariana no emprego novo' and follows her day.

questions.q: Why did Mariana get nervous?
options: The bus was going to the airport
She lost her phone on the bus
The bus did not come for forty minutes
Her boss called her and was angry
questions.explain: The driver said 'Vai para o aeroporto!', and then 'Mariana ficou nervosa'.

questions.q: What did Dona Sílvia do when Mariana called her?
options: She laughed and told Mariana to stay calm
She got angry and closed the shop
She drove across the city to get Mariana
She told Mariana to come back the next day
questions.explain: The text says 'Dona Sílvia riu e disse: “Calma!”'.

questions.q: What is Mariana going to do tomorrow?
options: Take a taxi from home to the shop
Ask the driver about every bus stop
Leave earlier and check the bus number
Start work one hour later than today
questions.explain: The last sentence says 'ela vai sair de casa mais cedo e vai ler o número do ônibus duas vezes'.

title: O último imperador do Brasil
text:
Dom Pedro II foi o segundo e último imperador do Brasil. Ele nasceu no Rio de Janeiro em 1825. Quando ele tinha só cinco anos, o pai dele, Dom Pedro I, voltou para a Europa. O menino ficou no Brasil e estudou muito, com vários professores. Em 1840, com apenas catorze anos, ele começou a governar o país.

Pedro II gostava muito de livros, de ciência e de línguas. Ele aprendeu a falar várias línguas e escrevia cartas para cientistas e escritores de outros países. Ele também gostava de fotografia e foi um dos primeiros brasileiros a ter uma máquina fotográfica. O imperador viajou muito e conheceu a Europa e os Estados Unidos.

Ele governou o Brasil por quase cinquenta anos. Em 1889, o país virou uma república, e a família imperial teve que ir morar na Europa. Pedro II morreu em Paris em 1891. Hoje, o palácio de verão dele, na cidade de Petrópolis, é um museu muito visitado.
translation:
Dom Pedro II was the second and last emperor of Brazil. He was born in Rio de Janeiro in 1825. When he was only five years old, his father, Dom Pedro I, went back to Europe. The boy stayed in Brazil and studied hard with several teachers. In 1840, at only fourteen, he began to rule the country.

Pedro II loved books, science and languages. He learned to speak several languages and wrote letters to scientists and writers from other countries. He also liked photography and was one of the first Brazilians to own a camera. The emperor traveled a lot and visited Europe and the United States.

He ruled Brazil for almost fifty years. In 1889, the country became a republic, and the imperial family had to go and live in Europe. Pedro II died in Paris in 1891. Today, his summer palace, in the city of Petrópolis, is a museum that many people visit.

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The history of the city of Petrópolis
How the first trains came to Brazil
The childhood of Dom Pedro I
The life of Brazil's last emperor
questions.explain: The text tells the life of Pedro II, 'o segundo e último imperador do Brasil', from 1825 to 1891.

questions.q: How old was Pedro II when he began to rule Brazil?
options: Five years old
Fourteen years old
Eighteen years old
Fifty years old
questions.explain: The text says 'Em 1840, com apenas catorze anos, ele começou a governar o país'.

questions.q: Which hobby of Pedro II does the text mention?
options: Painting
Playing the piano
Football
Photography
questions.explain: The text says 'Ele também gostava de fotografia'.

questions.q: Where did Pedro II die?
options: In Rio de Janeiro
In Petrópolis
In Paris
In Lisbon
questions.explain: The text says 'Pedro II morreu em Paris em 1891'.

title: A música de Chiquinha Gonzaga
text:
Chiquinha Gonzaga nasceu no Rio de Janeiro em 1847. Desde criança, ela adorava música e tocava piano muito bem. Com apenas onze anos, ela compôs a primeira música. Aos dezesseis anos, ela se casou, mas o marido não gostava da música dela. Então, ela se separou dele, uma coisa muito rara para uma mulher naquela época.

Para ganhar dinheiro, Chiquinha deu aulas de piano e tocou em festas e em lojas de música. Em 1877, uma polca dela fez muito sucesso na cidade. Depois, ela escreveu músicas para o teatro e, em 1885, foi a primeira mulher a dirigir uma orquestra no Brasil.

Em 1899, ela compôs “Ó Abre Alas”, considerada a primeira marchinha de carnaval. Até hoje, muitas pessoas cantam essa música no carnaval. Chiquinha morreu em 1935, com 87 anos, e deixou cerca de duas mil músicas. O Dia Nacional da Música Popular Brasileira é 17 de outubro, o dia do aniversário dela.
translation:
Chiquinha Gonzaga was born in Rio de Janeiro in 1847. Since she was a child, she loved music and played the piano very well. At only eleven, she composed her first song. At sixteen, she got married, but her husband didn't like her music. So she separated from him, something very rare for a woman at that time.

To earn money, Chiquinha gave piano lessons and played at parties and in music shops. In 1877, one of her polkas was a great success in the city. Later, she wrote music for the theater and, in 1885, she became the first woman to conduct an orchestra in Brazil.

In 1899, she composed “Ó Abre Alas”, considered the first carnival marchinha. Even today, many people sing this song at carnival. Chiquinha died in 1935, at the age of 87, and left about two thousand pieces of music. The National Day of Brazilian Popular Music is October 17, her birthday.

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The life and work of a Brazilian composer
The history of carnival in Rio de Janeiro
How to learn to play the piano
A famous theater in Rio de Janeiro
questions.explain: The text tells the life of Chiquinha Gonzaga, from her birth in 1847, and the music she composed.

questions.q: Why did Chiquinha separate from her husband?
options: He wanted to move to Portugal
He sold her piano
He did not like her music
He did not want to have children
questions.explain: The text says 'o marido não gostava da música dela. Então, ela se separou dele'.

questions.q: What was Chiquinha the first woman in Brazil to do?
options: Teach piano at a school
Conduct an orchestra
Sing at carnival
Open a music shop
questions.explain: The text says she 'foi a primeira mulher a dirigir uma orquestra no Brasil'.

questions.q: What is celebrated on October 17?
options: The first day of the carnival in Rio
A big piano contest for young people
The end of the school year in Brazil
Brazil's National Day of Popular Music
questions.explain: The last sentence says 'O Dia Nacional da Música Popular Brasileira é 17 de outubro'.

title: A capivara
text:
A capivara é o maior roedor do mundo. Ela é parente do porquinho-da-índia, mas é muito maior: um adulto pode pesar mais de cinquenta quilos. O nome “capivara” vem do tupi e quer dizer “comedor de capim”.

As capivaras vivem na América do Sul, sempre perto de rios e lagos. Elas nadam muito bem, porque têm uma pele fina entre os dedos. Os olhos, as orelhas e o nariz ficam no alto da cabeça. Por isso, a capivara consegue ver e respirar quando quase todo o corpo está dentro da água. Ela também pode ficar até cinco minutos debaixo d'água.

As capivaras comem capim e plantas aquáticas. Elas vivem em grupos de dez a vinte animais e passam as horas mais quentes do dia na água ou na lama. No Brasil, é comum ver capivaras em parques de cidades grandes, como Curitiba e São Paulo.
translation:
The capybara is the largest rodent in the world. It is a relative of the guinea pig, but it is much bigger: an adult can weigh more than fifty kilos. The name “capivara” comes from Tupi and means “grass eater”.

Capybaras live in South America, always near rivers and lakes. They swim very well because they have thin skin between their toes. Their eyes, ears and nose are on the top of the head. That is why a capybara can see and breathe when almost its whole body is in the water. It can also stay underwater for up to five minutes.

Capybaras eat grass and water plants. They live in groups of ten to twenty animals and spend the hottest hours of the day in the water or in the mud. In Brazil, it is common to see capybaras in parks in big cities, such as Curitiba and São Paulo.

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to keep a capybara as a pet
The parks of Curitiba and São Paulo
Facts about the world's largest rodent
Words that come from the Tupi language
questions.explain: The text gives facts about the capybara, 'o maior roedor do mundo'.

questions.q: Why do capybaras swim well?
options: They have thin skin between their toes
They have very long and strong tails
They are very small and light animals
They eat only plants that grow in water
questions.explain: The text says 'Elas nadam muito bem, porque têm uma pele fina entre os dedos'.

questions.q: How long can a capybara stay underwater?
options: Up to one minute
Up to five minutes
Up to fifteen minutes
Up to one hour
questions.explain: The text says 'Ela também pode ficar até cinco minutos debaixo d'água'.

questions.q: What does the name “capivara” mean?
options: Big rat
River swimmer
Mud lover
Grass eater
questions.explain: The name 'quer dizer “comedor de capim”', and capim means grass.

topic: the cicada and the ant fable
title: A cigarra e a formiga
text:
Era uma vez uma cigarra e uma formiga. Durante todo o verão, a cigarra cantava e dançava debaixo de uma árvore. A formiga, ao contrário, trabalhava o dia inteiro. Ela levava folhas e sementes para a casa dela, embaixo da terra.

Um dia, a cigarra perguntou: “Por que você trabalha tanto? O dia está lindo! Venha cantar comigo!” A formiga respondeu: “Não posso. Estou guardando comida para o inverno.” A cigarra riu e continuou a cantar.

Alguns meses depois, o inverno chegou. Fez muito frio, e a neve cobriu o campo. A cigarra não tinha casa nem comida. Com fome, ela foi até a casa da formiga e pediu ajuda. A formiga perguntou: “O que você fez no verão?” “Eu cantei”, respondeu a cigarra. A formiga pensou e deu um pouco de comida para ela. Mas disse: “No próximo verão, você vai cantar e também trabalhar.” E a cigarra aprendeu a lição.
translation:
Once upon a time there was a cicada and an ant. All summer long, the cicada sang and danced under a tree. The ant, on the other hand, worked all day. She carried leaves and seeds to her home under the ground.

One day, the cicada asked: “Why do you work so much? The day is beautiful! Come and sing with me!” The ant answered: “I can't. I'm saving food for the winter.” The cicada laughed and went on singing.

A few months later, winter arrived. It was very cold, and snow covered the field. The cicada had no home and no food. Hungry, she went to the ant's house and asked for help. The ant asked: “What did you do in the summer?” “I sang,” answered the cicada. The ant thought about it and gave her a little food. But she said: “Next summer, you are going to sing and also work.” And the cicada learned her lesson.

questions.q: What is the main lesson of the story?
options: You should never laugh at your friends
It is important to prepare for the future
Ants and cicadas can never be friends
Winter is the best season of the year
questions.explain: The story ends with the words 'E a cigarra aprendeu a lição'.

questions.q: What did the ant do during the summer?
options: She sang and danced under a tree all day
She slept every afternoon under the ground
She traveled to a warmer place by the sea
She carried leaves and seeds to her home
questions.explain: The text says the ant 'levava folhas e sementes para a casa dela'.

questions.q: Why did the cicada go to the ant's house?
options: She was hungry and had no food
She wanted to sing for the ant
She wanted to give the ant a present
She was looking for her friends
questions.explain: The text says 'A cigarra não tinha casa nem comida. Com fome, ela foi até a casa da formiga'.

questions.q: What did the ant tell the cicada at the end?
options: To leave the house right away
To sing all winter in the house
To sing and also work next summer
To find another ant to help her
questions.explain: The ant says 'No próximo verão, você vai cantar e também trabalhar'.

topic: Charles Miller brings football to Brazil
title: Como o futebol chegou ao Brasil
text:
Charles Miller nasceu em São Paulo em 1874. O pai dele era escocês, e a mãe era brasileira. Ainda criança, Charles foi estudar na Inglaterra. Lá, ele conheceu um esporte muito popular entre os ingleses: o futebol. Ele começou a jogar na escola e logo virou um bom jogador.

Em 1894, Charles voltou para o Brasil. Na mala, ele trouxe duas bolas, uniformes, uma bomba de ar e um livro com as regras do jogo. Em São Paulo, ele ensinou o futebol aos amigos. Em abril de 1895, aconteceu a primeira partida organizada do país, entre trabalhadores de uma ferrovia e de uma empresa de gás. O time de Charles, o da ferrovia, ganhou por quatro a dois.

No começo, o futebol era um esporte de pessoas ricas, mas depois ficou popular em todo o Brasil. O país ganhou a Copa do Mundo pela primeira vez em 1958. Hoje, uma praça em São Paulo tem o nome de Charles Miller.
translation:
Charles Miller was born in São Paulo in 1874. His father was Scottish, and his mother was Brazilian. As a child, Charles went to study in England. There, he discovered a sport that was very popular among the English: football. He began to play at school and soon became a good player.

In 1894, Charles returned to Brazil. In his suitcase, he brought two balls, uniforms, an air pump and a book with the rules of the game. In São Paulo, he taught football to his friends. In April 1895, the first organized match in the country took place, between workers from a railway and from a gas company. Charles's team, the railway one, won four to two.

At first, football was a sport for rich people, but later it became popular all over Brazil. The country won the World Cup for the first time in 1958. Today, a square in São Paulo bears Charles Miller's name.

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The life of a Scottish engineer
The history of the World Cup
How football arrived in Brazil
How to become a good player
questions.explain: The text tells how Charles Miller brought football to Brazil, where 'ele ensinou o futebol aos amigos'.

questions.q: Where did Charles learn to play football?
options: In Scotland
In England
In São Paulo
In Sweden
questions.explain: Charles went to study in England, and there 'ele conheceu ... o futebol. Ele começou a jogar na escola'.

questions.q: What did Charles bring in his suitcase?
options: Balls, uniforms, a pump and a rule book
Shoes, a camera and some old maps
Books about the history of Brazil
A trophy and photos of his school team
questions.explain: The text says 'ele trouxe duas bolas, uniformes, uma bomba de ar e um livro com as regras do jogo'.

questions.q: When did Brazil win its first World Cup?
questions.explain: The text says 'O país ganhou a Copa do Mundo pela primeira vez em 1958'.

title: Uma língua, dois países
text:
O português é a língua oficial do Brasil e de Portugal, mas não é exatamente igual nos dois países. O Brasil tem mais de duzentos milhões de habitantes, e Portugal tem cerca de dez milhões. Por isso, a maioria das pessoas que falam português no mundo é brasileira.

Muitas palavras são diferentes. No Brasil, as pessoas pegam o ônibus ou o trem. Em Portugal, elas usam o autocarro ou o comboio. Um brasileiro toma café da manhã e guarda o leite na geladeira. Um português toma o pequeno-almoço e guarda o leite no frigorífico. Até o telefone que levamos no bolso muda de nome: no Brasil é celular, e em Portugal é telemóvel.

A pronúncia também é diferente. Em Portugal, muitas vogais quase desaparecem quando as pessoas falam. No Brasil, as vogais são mais claras. Além disso, os brasileiros usam muito “você”, e os portugueses usam mais “tu” com os amigos. Mas, com um pouco de atenção, brasileiros e portugueses se entendem bem.
translation:
Portuguese is the official language of Brazil and Portugal, but it is not exactly the same in the two countries. Brazil has more than two hundred million inhabitants, and Portugal has about ten million. That is why most people in the world who speak Portuguese are Brazilian.

Many words are different. In Brazil, people take the ônibus (bus) or the trem (train). In Portugal, they use the autocarro or the comboio. A Brazilian has café da manhã (breakfast) and keeps the milk in the geladeira (fridge). A Portuguese person has pequeno-almoço and keeps the milk in the frigorífico. Even the phone we carry in our pocket changes its name: in Brazil it is celular, and in Portugal it is telemóvel.

The pronunciation is different too. In Portugal, many vowels almost disappear when people speak. In Brazil, the vowels are clearer. Also, Brazilians use “você” (you) a lot, and Portuguese people use “tu” more with friends. But with a little attention, Brazilians and Portuguese people understand each other well.

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How Portuguese differs in Brazil and Portugal
Why Portuguese is a hard language to learn
The long history of the Portuguese language
How to travel by bus and train in Portugal
questions.explain: The text compares the words and pronunciation of Portuguese 'nos dois países', Brazil and Portugal.

questions.q: What do people in Portugal call a train?
options: Autocarro
Comboio
Telemóvel
Frigorífico
questions.explain: Brazilians take 'o ônibus ou o trem', and in Portugal people use 'o autocarro ou o comboio', so comboio is a train.

questions.q: Why are most Portuguese speakers in the world Brazilian?
options: Brazilian Portuguese is easier to learn
Many Portuguese people speak other languages
Brazil has more schools than Portugal
Brazil has many more people than Portugal
questions.explain: Brazil has 'mais de duzentos milhões de habitantes' and Portugal 'cerca de dez milhões'; 'Por isso' most speakers are Brazilian.

questions.q: What does the text say about vowels in Portugal?
options: Many of them almost disappear in speech
They are clearer than in Brazil
They are always written with accents
They sound the same as in Spanish
questions.explain: The text says 'Em Portugal, muitas vogais quase desaparecem quando as pessoas falam'.

title: Os nossos ossos
text:
O corpo de um adulto tem 206 ossos. Um bebê nasce com mais ossos, cerca de trezentos, mas alguns ossos se juntam quando a criança cresce. Mais da metade dos nossos ossos fica nas mãos e nos pés.

Os ossos têm funções muito importantes. Eles sustentam o corpo e nos ajudam a andar e a correr. Eles também protegem os órgãos: o crânio protege o cérebro, e as costelas protegem o coração e os pulmões. Dentro de alguns ossos, há uma parte mole que produz as células do sangue. O maior osso do corpo é o fêmur, na coxa. O menor fica dentro do ouvido e tem só três milímetros.

Os ossos estão vivos. Quando uma pessoa quebra um osso, ele se recupera em algumas semanas. Para ter ossos fortes, é bom comer alimentos com cálcio, como leite, queijo e verduras. O sol também ajuda, porque o corpo produz vitamina D com a luz do sol. E, claro, é importante fazer exercício.
translation:
An adult's body has 206 bones. A baby is born with more bones, about three hundred, but some bones join together as the child grows. More than half of our bones are in the hands and feet.

Bones have very important jobs. They support the body and help us walk and run. They also protect the organs: the skull protects the brain, and the ribs protect the heart and lungs. Inside some bones, there is a soft part that makes blood cells. The largest bone in the body is the femur, in the thigh. The smallest is inside the ear and is only three millimeters long.

Bones are alive. When a person breaks a bone, it heals in a few weeks. To have strong bones, it is good to eat foods with calcium, such as milk, cheese and leafy green vegetables. The sun helps too, because the body makes vitamin D with sunlight. And, of course, it is important to exercise.

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How doctors treat a broken leg
Why babies need to drink milk
How muscles help us run fast
Facts about the bones in our body
questions.explain: The text explains how many bones we have, what they do and how to keep them strong.

questions.q: How many bones does an adult have?
questions.explain: The first sentence says 'O corpo de um adulto tem 206 ossos'.

questions.q: What do the ribs protect?
options: The brain and the eyes
The hands and the feet
The heart and the lungs
The stomach and the ears
questions.explain: The text says 'as costelas protegem o coração e os pulmões'.

questions.q: Why does the sun help our bones?
options: The body makes vitamin D with sunlight
Sunlight makes our bones grow longer
The sun puts calcium into our food
Warm bones heal faster than cold bones
questions.explain: The text says 'O sol também ajuda, porque o corpo produz vitamina D com a luz do sol'.

title: Notícias do Rio
text:
Oi, Camila! Cheguei ao Rio de Janeiro na sexta-feira com meus pais. A cidade é linda e muito quente! No sábado de manhã, nós fomos à praia de Copacabana. Eu nadei no mar, tomei água de coco e comi milho cozido na areia. À tarde, choveu um pouco, então visitamos um museu de arte.

Ontem, subimos o Pão de Açúcar de bondinho. Lá de cima, vimos as praias, as montanhas e os barcos na baía. A vista é maravilhosa! Meu pai tirou mais de cem fotos! À noite, jantamos num restaurante pequeno perto do hotel. Eu comi um peixe delicioso com arroz e salada.

Amanhã, vamos conhecer o Jardim Botânico, porque minha mãe adora plantas. Na quinta-feira, vamos ver um jogo de futebol no Maracanã, um estádio enorme e muito famoso. Eu estou muito animada! Volto para Belo Horizonte no domingo e vou te contar tudo. Um beijo, Júlia.
translation:
Hi, Camila! I arrived in Rio de Janeiro on Friday with my parents. The city is beautiful and very hot! On Saturday morning, we went to Copacabana beach. I swam in the sea, drank coconut water and ate boiled corn on the sand. In the afternoon, it rained a little, so we visited an art museum.

Yesterday, we went up Sugarloaf Mountain by cable car. From the top, we saw the beaches, the mountains and the boats in the bay. The view is wonderful! My dad took more than a hundred photos! In the evening, we had dinner at a small restaurant near the hotel. I ate a delicious fish with rice and salad.

Tomorrow, we are going to visit the Botanical Garden, because my mom loves plants. On Thursday, we are going to see a football match at the Maracanã, a huge and very famous stadium. I'm very excited! I'm going back to Belo Horizonte on Sunday, and I'll tell you everything. Love, Júlia.

questions.q: Why did Júlia write this message?
options: To invite Camila to a football match
To tell her friend about her trip to Rio
To ask Camila for a good restaurant
To say that she is moving to Rio
questions.explain: Júlia tells Camila what she did and is going to do in Rio, and she ends with 'vou te contar tudo'.

questions.q: What did the family do when it rained on Saturday?
options: They went back to the hotel
They went up Sugarloaf Mountain
They had lunch on the beach
They visited an art museum
questions.explain: The text says 'À tarde, choveu um pouco, então visitamos um museu de arte'.

questions.q: How did they go up Sugarloaf Mountain?
options: On foot
By car
By cable car
By helicopter
questions.explain: The text says 'subimos o Pão de Açúcar de bondinho', and a bondinho is a cable car.

questions.q: Why are they going to visit the Botanical Garden?
options: It is very near their hotel
Júlia's dad wants to take photos
It is free on Tuesdays
Júlia's mom loves plants
questions.explain: The text says 'vamos conhecer o Jardim Botânico, porque minha mãe adora plantas'.

title: A bandeira do Brasil
text:
A bandeira do Brasil que conhecemos hoje é de 1889. No dia 15 de novembro daquele ano, o Brasil deixou de ser um império e virou uma república. Quatro dias depois, no dia 19 de novembro, o país ganhou uma bandeira nova. Por isso, o Dia da Bandeira é 19 de novembro.

As cores verde e amarela vêm da bandeira do Império, mas muitas pessoas dizem que o verde representa as florestas e o amarelo representa o ouro. No meio da bandeira, há um círculo azul com estrelas. Ele mostra o céu do Rio de Janeiro na manhã de 15 de novembro de 1889.

Cada estrela representa um estado ou o Distrito Federal, onde fica Brasília. Em 1889, a bandeira tinha 21 estrelas, e hoje ela tem 27. Quando o país cria um estado novo, a bandeira ganha mais uma estrela. Na faixa branca, está escrito “Ordem e Progresso”. Essa frase veio das ideias de um filósofo francês, Auguste Comte.
translation:
The flag of Brazil that we know today is from 1889. On November 15 of that year, Brazil stopped being an empire and became a republic. Four days later, on November 19, the country got a new flag. That is why Flag Day is November 19.

The colors green and yellow come from the flag of the Empire, but many people say that the green represents the forests and the yellow represents gold. In the middle of the flag, there is a blue circle with stars. It shows the sky over Rio de Janeiro on the morning of November 15, 1889.

Each star represents a state or the Federal District, where Brasília is. In 1889, the flag had 21 stars, and today it has 27. When the country creates a new state, the flag gets one more star. On the white band are the words “Ordem e Progresso” (Order and Progress). This phrase came from the ideas of a French philosopher, Auguste Comte.

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The story and meaning of Brazil's flag
How Brazil became an empire in 1889
The life of a French philosopher
How new states are created in Brazil
questions.explain: The text explains when the flag was created and what its colors, stars and words mean.

questions.q: Why is Flag Day on November 19?
options: Brazil became a republic on that day
A new state was created on that day
Auguste Comte was born on that day
The country got its new flag on that day
questions.explain: The text says 'no dia 19 de novembro, o país ganhou uma bandeira nova. Por isso, o Dia da Bandeira é 19 de novembro'.

questions.q: What does the blue circle show?
options: The ocean along the coast of Brazil
The great rivers of the Amazon
The sky over Rio on a special morning
A map of all the Brazilian states
questions.explain: The text says the circle 'mostra o céu do Rio de Janeiro na manhã de 15 de novembro de 1889'.

questions.q: How many stars did the flag have in 1889?
questions.explain: The text says 'Em 1889, a bandeira tinha 21 estrelas'.

title: Um teatro na floresta
text:
No meio da floresta amazônica, na cidade de Manaus, existe um teatro muito bonito: o Teatro Amazonas. Ele abriu as portas no dia 31 de dezembro de 1896.

Naquela época, Manaus era uma cidade rica. A Europa e os Estados Unidos compravam muita borracha, e essa borracha vinha das árvores da Amazônia. Com o dinheiro da borracha, a cidade construiu ruas, praças, um porto e esse teatro elegante. Muitos materiais vieram da Europa de navio: o mármore veio da Itália, e as telhas coloridas da cúpula vieram da França. A cúpula tem milhares dessas peças, nas cores da bandeira do Brasil.

No começo do século XX, a borracha da Ásia ficou mais barata, e Manaus perdeu muito dinheiro. Mas o teatro continuou lá. Hoje, ele tem cerca de setecentos lugares e recebe concertos, balés e um festival de ópera muito conhecido. Muitos turistas visitam o teatro quando viajam para a Amazônia.
translation:
In the middle of the Amazon rainforest, in the city of Manaus, there is a very beautiful theater: the Amazon Theatre. It opened its doors on December 31, 1896.

At that time, Manaus was a rich city. Europe and the United States bought a lot of rubber, and this rubber came from the trees of the Amazon. With the money from rubber, the city built streets, squares, a port and this elegant theater. Many materials came from Europe by ship: the marble came from Italy, and the colorful tiles of the dome came from France. The dome has thousands of these pieces, in the colors of the Brazilian flag.

At the beginning of the twentieth century, rubber from Asia became cheaper, and Manaus lost a lot of money. But the theater remained. Today, it has about seven hundred seats and hosts concerts, ballets and a well-known opera festival. Many tourists visit the theater when they travel to the Amazon.

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Wild animals of the Amazon rainforest
A famous theater in the Amazon
The history of opera in Europe
A long trip by ship from France
questions.explain: The text describes 'um teatro muito bonito: o Teatro Amazonas', in the city of Manaus.

questions.q: Why was Manaus rich at that time?
options: Other countries bought its rubber
It had many big gold mines nearby
Many tourists visited its theater
It sold a lot of coffee to Europe
questions.explain: The text says 'A Europa e os Estados Unidos compravam muita borracha', and the city grew 'com o dinheiro da borracha'.

questions.q: Where did the marble come from?
options: From France
From Italy
From Asia
From the Amazon
questions.explain: The text says 'o mármore veio da Itália'.

questions.q: How many seats does the theater have today?
options: About seventy
About two thousand
About seven thousand
About seven hundred
questions.explain: The text says 'Hoje, ele tem cerca de setecentos lugares'.

topic: sea turtles nesting on Brazilian beaches
title: As tartarugas marinhas
text:
No mundo, existem sete espécies de tartarugas marinhas, e cinco delas vivem no litoral do Brasil. Essas tartarugas passam quase a vida toda no mar. Normalmente, só as fêmeas saem da água, e só para botar ovos.

No Brasil, a maioria das tartarugas bota ovos entre setembro e março. As fêmeas chegam às praias à noite, e muitas voltam para a mesma praia onde nasceram. Cada fêmea cava um buraco na areia, bota cerca de cem ovos e volta para o mar. Os ovos ficam na areia quente por uns dois meses. A temperatura da areia decide se os filhotes vão ser machos ou fêmeas. Quando a areia está mais quente, nascem mais fêmeas.

Os filhotes saem da areia, geralmente à noite, e vão rápido para o mar. Eles seguem a luz da lua e das estrelas na água. Por isso, as luzes fortes perto da praia são um problema: os filhotes ficam confusos e vão na direção errada.
translation:
There are seven species of sea turtles in the world, and five of them live along the coast of Brazil. These turtles spend almost their whole lives in the sea. Normally, only the females leave the water, and only to lay eggs.

In Brazil, most turtles lay their eggs between September and March. The females arrive at the beaches at night, and many return to the same beach where they were born. Each female digs a hole in the sand, lays about a hundred eggs and goes back to the sea. The eggs stay in the warm sand for about two months. The temperature of the sand decides whether the babies will be male or female. When the sand is warmer, more females are born.

The babies come out of the sand, usually at night, and go quickly to the sea. They follow the light of the moon and the stars on the water. That is why strong lights near the beach are a problem: the babies get confused and go the wrong way.

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why sea turtles can live for many years
The best beaches in Brazil for swimming
How sea turtles lay eggs and are born
How fishermen work on the coast of Brazil
questions.explain: The text explains how each female 'cava um buraco na areia' for her eggs and what happens to them.

questions.q: How many eggs does a female lay at one time?
options: About ten
About fifty
About a hundred
About a thousand
questions.explain: The text says each female 'bota cerca de cem ovos'.

questions.q: What decides if the babies will be male or female?
options: The temperature of the sand
The size of the mother turtle
The depth of the hole in the sand
The light of the moon at night
questions.explain: The text says 'A temperatura da areia decide se os filhotes vão ser machos ou fêmeas'.

questions.q: Why are strong lights near the beach a problem?
options: The mothers cannot find the beach
The babies go in the wrong direction
The fish swim far away from the beach
The eggs break more easily at night
questions.explain: The text says that because of the lights 'os filhotes ficam confusos e vão na direção errada'.

title: O bolo de aniversário
text:
No sábado, era aniversário da mãe do Téo. Ela foi trabalhar de manhã, e o Téo, que tem nove anos, teve uma ideia: fazer um bolo de chocolate com o pai. Eles encontraram uma receita na internet e foram ao supermercado comprar os ingredientes.

Em casa, eles misturaram farinha, açúcar, ovos, leite e chocolate. O Téo quebrou os ovos, e o pai mexeu a massa. A cozinha ficou uma bagunça: tinha farinha no chão, na mesa e até no cabelo do Téo! Depois, eles colocaram o bolo no forno. Mas, quarenta minutos depois, o bolo saiu baixo e duro. Eles esqueceram o fermento!

Nesse momento, a mãe chegou em casa. Ela viu a cozinha suja e o bolo estranho e começou a rir. Depois, abraçou os dois e disse: “É o melhor presente do mundo!” À noite, a família comeu o bolo com sorvete, e todo mundo gostou. No próximo ano, o Téo vai ler a receita com mais atenção.
translation:
On Saturday, it was Téo's mother's birthday. She went to work in the morning, and Téo, who is nine years old, had an idea: to make a chocolate cake with his dad. They found a recipe on the internet and went to the supermarket to buy the ingredients.

At home, they mixed flour, sugar, eggs, milk and chocolate. Téo broke the eggs, and his dad stirred the batter. The kitchen became a mess: there was flour on the floor, on the table and even in Téo's hair! Then they put the cake in the oven. But forty minutes later, the cake came out flat and hard. They had forgotten the baking powder!

At that moment, his mother came home. She saw the dirty kitchen and the strange cake, and she started to laugh. Then she hugged them both and said: “It's the best present in the world!” In the evening, the family ate the cake with ice cream, and everybody liked it. Next year, Téo is going to read the recipe more carefully.

questions.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: A boy and his dad bake a birthday cake
A family has dinner at a restaurant
A mother teaches her son to cook
A boy buys a present at the market
questions.explain: Téo and his dad decide 'fazer um bolo de chocolate' for his mother's birthday.

questions.q: Where was Téo's mother in the morning?
options: At the supermarket
At a friend's house
In the kitchen
At work
questions.explain: The text says 'Ela foi trabalhar de manhã'.

questions.q: Why did the cake come out flat and hard?
options: They put in too much sugar
The oven was much too hot
They forgot the baking powder
Téo broke too many eggs
questions.explain: The text says the cake 'saiu baixo e duro. Eles esqueceram o fermento!'

questions.q: What did the mother do when she saw the kitchen?
options: She started to laugh
She got very angry
She cleaned it alone
She called her sister
questions.explain: The text says 'Ela viu a cozinha suja e o bolo estranho e começou a rir'.

title: Os Jogos Olímpicos
text:
Os primeiros Jogos Olímpicos aconteceram na Grécia antiga, em um lugar chamado Olímpia, há quase três mil anos. Os jogos aconteciam a cada quatro anos. No começo, havia só uma prova: uma corrida curta. Depois, os gregos incluíram outras provas, como luta, salto e lançamento de disco. Os atletas eram só homens gregos, e os vencedores ganhavam uma coroa de folhas de oliveira.

Os jogos antigos acabaram há cerca de 1.600 anos. Muitos séculos depois, um francês chamado Pierre de Coubertin quis trazer os jogos de volta. Assim, em 1896, Atenas recebeu os primeiros Jogos Olímpicos modernos. Quatro anos depois, em Paris, as mulheres participaram pela primeira vez.

Hoje, atletas de quase todos os países do mundo participam dos jogos. O símbolo olímpico tem cinco anéis coloridos, que representam os continentes unidos pelo esporte. Em 2016, o Rio de Janeiro recebeu os Jogos Olímpicos. Foi a primeira vez que a América do Sul recebeu o evento.
translation:
The first Olympic Games took place in ancient Greece, at a place called Olympia, almost three thousand years ago. The games were held every four years. At first, there was only one event: a short race. Later, the Greeks added other events, such as wrestling, jumping and discus throwing. The athletes were only Greek men, and the winners received a crown of olive leaves.

The ancient games ended about 1,600 years ago. Many centuries later, a Frenchman named Pierre de Coubertin wanted to bring the games back. So, in 1896, Athens hosted the first modern Olympic Games. Four years later, in Paris, women took part for the first time.

Today, athletes from almost every country in the world take part in the games. The Olympic symbol has five colored rings, which represent the continents united by sport. In 2016, Rio de Janeiro hosted the Olympic Games. It was the first time that South America hosted the event.

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The life of Pierre de Coubertin
Sports in modern Greece
How to train for a short race
The history of the Olympic Games
questions.explain: The text tells the history of the Olympic Games, from ancient Greece to Rio de Janeiro in 2016.

questions.q: What did the winners of the ancient games receive?
options: A crown of olive leaves
A medal made of gold
A big bag of money
A small house in Olympia
questions.explain: The text says 'os vencedores ganhavam uma coroa de folhas de oliveira'.

questions.q: When did women take part in the Olympic Games for the first time?
options: In 1896, in Athens
In 1900, in Paris
In 2016, in Rio
In ancient Greece
questions.explain: The modern games began in 1896, and 'Quatro anos depois, em Paris, as mulheres participaram pela primeira vez'.

questions.q: What do the five rings represent?
options: The first five sports
The five cities of the games
The continents united by sport
The five winners of a race
questions.explain: The text says the rings 'representam os continentes unidos pelo esporte'.

topic: cordel poetry booklets of Northeast Brazil
title: A literatura de cordel
text:
A literatura de cordel é uma forma de poesia popular muito famosa no Nordeste do Brasil. Os poemas são impressos em livrinhos simples e baratos, chamados folhetos. O nome “cordel” quer dizer “corda fina”, porque, antigamente, os vendedores penduravam os folhetos em cordas nas feiras.

Os poemas de cordel contam histórias de amor, de animais, de viagens e de pessoas espertas. Muitas histórias são engraçadas. Os versos têm rima e ritmo, e por isso é fácil lembrar deles. Nas feiras, o poeta lia os versos em voz alta para chamar os clientes. Antigamente, muitas pessoas do interior não sabiam ler, mas conheciam as histórias porque ouviam os poetas.

Muitas capas de folhetos têm desenhos em preto e branco, feitos com uma técnica chamada xilogravura. Nessa técnica, o artista corta o desenho em um pedaço de madeira, coloca tinta e imprime no papel. Em 2018, o cordel virou patrimônio cultural do Brasil.
translation:
Cordel literature is a form of popular poetry that is very famous in the Northeast of Brazil. The poems are printed in simple, cheap little books called folhetos (booklets). The name “cordel” means “thin cord”, because in the old days sellers hung the booklets on cords at the markets.

Cordel poems tell stories about love, animals, journeys and clever people. Many stories are funny. The verses have rhyme and rhythm, and that is why they are easy to remember. At the markets, the poet read the verses aloud to attract customers. In the old days, many people in the countryside could not read, but they knew the stories because they listened to the poets.

Many booklet covers have black-and-white pictures, made with a technique called xilogravura (woodcut). In this technique, the artist cuts the picture into a piece of wood, puts ink on it and prints it on paper. In 2018, cordel became part of Brazil's cultural heritage.

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to write a good love letter
The life of a famous Brazilian poet
A tradition of popular poetry
The markets of the Northeast
questions.explain: The text describes literatura de cordel, 'uma forma de poesia popular' from the Northeast of Brazil.

questions.q: Where does the name “cordel” come from?
options: The name of the first cordel poet
A small town in the Northeast
The songs sung at the old markets
The cords used to hang the booklets
questions.explain: The text says 'cordel' means 'corda fina', because 'os vendedores penduravam os folhetos em cordas'.

questions.q: Why did poets read their verses aloud at the markets?
options: To teach children to write
To practice for a contest
Because the poets could not write
To attract customers
questions.explain: The text says 'o poeta lia os versos em voz alta para chamar os clientes'.

questions.q: What is a “xilogravura”?
options: A kind of poem with rhyme
A way to print pictures with wood
A small market in the countryside
A cheap kind of paper
questions.explain: The text explains that in xilogravura 'o artista corta o desenho em um pedaço de madeira, coloca tinta e imprime no papel'.

topic: the planets of the solar system
title: Os planetas do sistema solar
titleEn: The Planets of the Solar System
text:
O sistema solar tem o Sol e oito planetas. Os quatro planetas mais perto do Sol são Mercúrio, Vênus, Terra e Marte. Eles são pequenos e feitos de rocha. Os outros quatro, Júpiter, Saturno, Urano e Netuno, são enormes e feitos principalmente de gás e gelo.

Mercúrio é o menor planeta e o mais perto do Sol, mas não é o mais quente. O planeta mais quente é Vênus, porque a atmosfera dele é muito densa e guarda o calor. A Terra é o terceiro planeta e o único planeta com vida que conhecemos. Marte é chamado de “planeta vermelho”, porque o solo dele tem muita ferrugem.

Júpiter é o maior de todos: mais de mil Terras cabem dentro dele! Saturno tem anéis lindos, feitos de gelo e pedras. Urano e Netuno ficam muito longe e são muito frios. Até 2006, Plutão também era um planeta, mas hoje os cientistas o chamam de planeta anão.
translation:
The solar system has the Sun and eight planets. The four planets closest to the Sun are Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars. They are small and made of rock. The other four, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, are huge and made mainly of gas and ice.

Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the Sun, but it is not the hottest. The hottest planet is Venus, because its atmosphere is very thick and keeps the heat in. Earth is the third planet and the only planet with life that we know of. Mars is called the “red planet” because its soil has a lot of rust.

Jupiter is the largest of all: more than a thousand Earths fit inside it! Saturn has beautiful rings made of ice and rock. Uranus and Neptune are very far away and very cold. Until 2006, Pluto was also a planet, but today scientists call it a dwarf planet.

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The planets that go around the Sun
How scientists plan trips to Mars
Why the Sun is so big and hot
How the Moon moves around the Earth
questions.explain: The text describes the planets of 'O sistema solar' and what each one is like.

questions.q: Which planet is the hottest?
options: Mercury
Venus
Mars
Jupiter
questions.explain: The text says 'O planeta mais quente é Vênus'.

questions.q: Why is Mars called the “red planet”?
options: Its soil has a lot of rust
It is very close to the Sun
It has red rings around it
It is the hottest planet
questions.explain: The text says Mars is the 'planeta vermelho' 'porque o solo dele tem muita ferrugem'.

questions.q: What happened to Pluto in 2006?
options: Scientists discovered it
It became the ninth planet
It lost its icy rings
It stopped being a planet
questions.explain: The text says 'Até 2006, Plutão também era um planeta, mas hoje os cientistas o chamam de planeta anão'.

title: A carteira perdida
text:
Numa tarde de outubro, Pedro estava voltando da faculdade, em Porto Alegre, quando viu uma carteira marrom em um banco da praça. Ele olhou em volta, mas não tinha ninguém por perto. Dentro da carteira, havia dinheiro, alguns documentos e uma foto antiga de um casal jovem. Num documento, estava o nome do dono: Ernesto Lima.

Pedro também encontrou um endereço na carteira. Ele pegou um ônibus e foi até lá. Um senhor de cabelo branco abriu a porta e ficou muito feliz. “Essa foto é do meu casamento! Eu procurei a carteira o dia inteiro”, ele disse. Seu Ernesto quis dar dinheiro para o rapaz, mas Pedro não aceitou.

Então, o senhor contou que foi professor de violão por quarenta anos e ofereceu aulas grátis. Pedro sempre quis aprender a tocar e aceitou na hora. Agora, ele vai à casa de Seu Ernesto todas as quartas-feiras. No aniversário da mãe, ele vai tocar a primeira música para ela.
translation:
One afternoon in October, Pedro was coming back from university in Porto Alegre when he saw a brown wallet on a bench in the square. He looked around, but there was nobody nearby. Inside the wallet, there was money, some documents and an old photo of a young couple. On one document was the owner's name: Ernesto Lima.

Pedro also found an address in the wallet. He took a bus and went there. A white-haired man opened the door and was very happy. “This photo is from my wedding! I looked for the wallet all day,” he said. Seu Ernesto wanted to give the young man some money, but Pedro didn't accept.

Then the old man said that he had been a guitar teacher for forty years and offered free lessons. Pedro had always wanted to learn to play, and he accepted right away. Now he goes to Seu Ernesto's house every Wednesday. On his mother's birthday, he is going to play his first song for her.

questions.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: A student who loses his wallet on a bus
An old man who looks for his old photos
A student who returns a lost wallet
A teacher who opens a music school
questions.explain: Pedro finds 'uma carteira marrom' in the square and takes it back to its owner, Seu Ernesto.

questions.q: How did Pedro find the owner's address?
options: He found it in the wallet
He asked people in the square
He looked for it on the internet
A bus driver told him
questions.explain: The text says 'Pedro também encontrou um endereço na carteira'.

questions.q: What did Pedro do when Seu Ernesto offered him money?
options: He took it and said thank you
He gave it to his mother
He bought a guitar with it
He did not accept it
questions.explain: The text says 'Seu Ernesto quis dar dinheiro para o rapaz, mas Pedro não aceitou'.

questions.q: When does Pedro go to Seu Ernesto's house now?
options: Every Monday
Every Wednesday
Every weekend
Only in October
questions.explain: The text says 'ele vai à casa de Seu Ernesto todas as quartas-feiras'.

title: A história do chocolate
text:
O chocolate vem das sementes do cacau, uma árvore das florestas da América. Os frutos do cacau são grandes e crescem direto no tronco da árvore. Dentro deles, há muitas sementes, cobertas por uma polpa branca e doce. No Brasil, as pessoas fazem suco com essa polpa.

Há muitos séculos, os maias e os astecas, no México e na América Central, já usavam o cacau. Eles faziam uma bebida amarga com as sementes, água e pimenta. Essa bebida não tinha açúcar! Para os astecas, as sementes de cacau eram tão valiosas que funcionavam como dinheiro.

No século XVI, os espanhóis levaram o cacau para a Europa. Lá, as pessoas colocaram açúcar na bebida, e ela ficou muito popular, mas era cara, e só os ricos podiam tomar. No século XIX, novas máquinas permitiram fazer chocolate sólido, em barras, e os suíços criaram o chocolate ao leite. Hoje, o Brasil também produz cacau, principalmente nos estados da Bahia e do Pará.
translation:
Chocolate comes from the seeds of cacao, a tree from the forests of the Americas. Cacao fruits are big and grow directly on the tree trunk. Inside them, there are many seeds, covered by a sweet white pulp. In Brazil, people make juice from this pulp.

Many centuries ago, the Maya and the Aztecs, in Mexico and Central America, already used cacao. They made a bitter drink with the seeds, water and chili pepper. This drink had no sugar! For the Aztecs, cacao seeds were so valuable that they were used as money.

In the sixteenth century, the Spanish took cacao to Europe. There, people put sugar in the drink, and it became very popular, but it was expensive, and only rich people could drink it. In the nineteenth century, new machines made it possible to make solid chocolate in bars, and the Swiss created milk chocolate. Today, Brazil also produces cacao, mainly in the states of Bahia and Pará.

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How chocolate is made in factories
The history of chocolate
The life of the Maya in Mexico
Why fruit is good for our health
questions.explain: The text tells the story of chocolate, from the Maya and the Aztecs to Europe and Brazil today.

questions.q: What was special about the drink of the Maya and the Aztecs?
options: It was made with milk and honey
It was sweet and very cold
It was bitter and had no sugar
Only children could drink it
questions.explain: The text says 'Eles faziam uma bebida amarga' and 'Essa bebida não tinha açúcar!'

questions.q: How did the Aztecs use cacao seeds?
options: To make bread
To build houses
To feed animals
As money
questions.explain: The text says the seeds 'eram tão valiosas que funcionavam como dinheiro'.

questions.q: Who created milk chocolate?
options: The Spanish
The Aztecs
The Swiss
The Brazilians
questions.explain: The text says 'os suíços criaram o chocolate ao leite'.

title: Os Lençóis Maranhenses
text:
No estado do Maranhão, no Nordeste do Brasil, existe uma paisagem diferente de tudo: os Lençóis Maranhenses. São quilômetros e quilômetros de dunas de areia branca, perto do mar. Vistas de cima, as dunas parecem lençóis brancos em uma cama enorme. Por isso, o lugar tem esse nome.

A região parece um deserto, mas não é, porque lá chove muito. Entre janeiro e junho, a água da chuva fica entre as dunas e forma muitas lagoas azuis e verdes. A água dessas lagoas é limpa e morna. A melhor época para visitar é de junho a setembro, quando as lagoas estão cheias e o céu fica azul.

Os turistas geralmente ficam na cidade de Barreirinhas. De lá, eles vão de carro 4x4 até as dunas e depois caminham descalços na areia. Muitos nadam nas lagoas e ficam para ver o pôr do sol. Desde 1981, a área é um parque nacional.
translation:
In the state of Maranhão, in the Northeast of Brazil, there is a landscape unlike anything else: the Lençóis Maranhenses. There are kilometers and kilometers of white sand dunes near the sea. Seen from above, the dunes look like white sheets (lençóis) on an enormous bed. That is why the place has this name.

The area looks like a desert, but it isn't, because it rains a lot there. Between January and June, rainwater collects between the dunes and forms many blue and green lagoons. The water in these lagoons is clean and warm. The best time to visit is from June to September, when the lagoons are full and the sky is blue.

Tourists usually stay in the town of Barreirinhas. From there, they go to the dunes by 4x4 car and then walk barefoot on the sand. Many swim in the lagoons and stay to watch the sunset. Since 1981, the area has been a national park.

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: A long river in the Amazon
A big city on the coast of Maranhão
How to drive a car on the sand
Dunes and lagoons in Maranhão
questions.explain: The text describes 'uma paisagem diferente de tudo' in Maranhão, with its dunes and lagoons.

questions.q: Why does the place have the name “Lençóis”?
options: The dunes look like sheets on a bed
People there make sheets for beds
The lagoons are white like sheets
Tourists sleep on sheets on the sand
questions.explain: The text says 'as dunas parecem lençóis brancos em uma cama enorme. Por isso, o lugar tem esse nome'.

questions.q: Why is the area not a desert?
options: It snows there in winter
It has many tall trees
It rains a lot there

title: Como as plantas se alimentam
text:
Os animais precisam comer para viver, mas as plantas fazem a própria comida. Esse processo se chama fotossíntese. A palavra vem do grego: “foto” quer dizer “luz”, e “síntese” quer dizer “juntar”.

Para fazer a fotossíntese, a planta precisa de três coisas: luz do sol, água e gás carbônico. As raízes tiram a água da terra, e as folhas pegam o gás carbônico do ar por buracos muito pequenos. As folhas também têm clorofila, uma substância verde que captura a luz do sol. É por isso que as folhas são verdes!

Com a energia da luz, a planta transforma a água e o gás carbônico em açúcar, que é o alimento dela. Ao mesmo tempo, ela solta oxigênio no ar. Nós e os animais respiramos esse oxigênio. Os cientistas calculam que cerca de metade do oxigênio do planeta vem do mar, onde algas muito pequenas também fazem fotossíntese. Por isso, a fotossíntese é muito importante para a vida na Terra.
translation:
Animals need to eat to live, but plants make their own food. This process is called photosynthesis. The word comes from Greek: “photo” means “light”, and “synthesis” means “putting together”.

To carry out photosynthesis, a plant needs three things: sunlight, water and carbon dioxide. The roots take water from the soil, and the leaves take carbon dioxide from the air through very small holes. Leaves also have chlorophyll, a green substance that captures sunlight. That is why leaves are green!

With the energy of light, the plant turns water and carbon dioxide into sugar, which is its food. At the same time, it releases oxygen into the air. We and the animals breathe this oxygen. Scientists estimate that about half of the planet's oxygen comes from the sea, where very small algae also carry out photosynthesis. That is why photosynthesis is very important for life on Earth.
